white.$description: White — Page canvas, base card surface, nav background

cream.$description: Cream — Warm off-white section background, soft card fill — the secondary surface layer that gives the page its paper-like warmth

fog.$description: Fog — Elevated card surfaces and subtle section bands

ash.$description: Ash — Hairline borders, dividers, input underlines — the structural skeleton of the layout

stone.$description: Stone — Tertiary text, placeholder copy, disabled states

steel.$description: Steel — Secondary body text, helper copy, muted descriptions

graphite.$description: Graphite — Secondary body text on cream surfaces

charcoal.$description: Charcoal — Secondary body text, navigation labels, and subdued headings. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

warm-gray.$description: Warm Gray — SVG icon fills, subtle warm-toned decorative elements

espresso.$description: Espresso — Primary text on cream surfaces, dark card accents, outlined action borders — the warm alternative to pure black

midnight.$description: Midnight — Primary body and heading text on white, the dominant ink color

pure-black.$description: Pure Black — Primary headings, body text, and icon fills on light surfaces. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

deep-ink.$description: Deep Ink — Footer and nav text, dark surface accents

slate-blue.$description: Slate Blue — Muted blue-gray for section backgrounds, subdued text accents, and image overlay washes — adds cool depth without competing with the cobalt accent

warm-sand.$description: Warm Sand — Warm tan card surfaces, trust/social-proof section backgrounds — a near-gray with just enough warmth to echo the photography

cobalt-spark.$description: Cobalt Spark — Violet text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases. Do not promote it to the primary CTA color

emerald.$description: Emerald — Green text accent for links, tags, and emphasized short phrases. Use as a supporting accent, not as a status color

geist.$description: Sole typeface — used for everything from display headlines down to 10px micro-copy. Geist's geometric neutrality and tall x-height make it read as editorial without being cold.
